title: Fever or respiratory symptoms
summary: Reported fever, cough or feeling unwell. A respiratory infection is possible if the overall picture is consistent. Body temperature must be measured with an independent source; the urine sample temperature describes the sample, not the body. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. No clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

immediate.text: Fever or respiratory symptoms with warning signs (severe breathing difficulty, new confusion or stiff neck): emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Loosen tight clothing and do not eat or drink while you are short of breath.

review.text: Fever, cough or feeling unwell without warning signs: rest, drink fluids and monitor.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Remove extra clothing; wear a light layer.
Measure body temperature with a thermometer and record the value and time.
If the fever lasts more than 48 to 72 hours or stays above 39.4 °C, record it in the report as a priority.

candidates.label: Respiratory infection
candidates.minimum_evidence: Fever or chills together with cough.
